title: Feature: Trip Builder for Multi-Leg Itineraries
author: Max-Jesch
body:
# Feature: Trip Builder for Multi-Leg Itineraries

**Problem:**
The current booking process only supports searching for and booking single flights. Users cannot create complex, multi-leg trips, view combined transit details, or see a consolidated price breakdown for an entire itinerary. This limits the platform's utility for users planning anything beyond simple one-way or round-trip journeys.

**Proposed Solution:**
Introduce a "Trip Builder" or "My Itinerary" feature. This would allow users to select and combine multiple flight legs into a single trip plan. The interface should display aggregated trip information, including total travel time, layover durations between legs, and a clear, itemized price breakdown for the entire itinerary before proceeding to payment.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Users can search for and add multiple individual flights to an itinerary.
- The itinerary view displays a list of all selected flight legs in chronological order.
- The UI shows the total transit time for the entire trip.
- The UI displays the duration of each layover between connecting flights.
- A consolidated price breakdown is visible, showing the cost of each leg and the total price.
- Users can proceed to a single payment step for the entire itinerary.
- Users can remove flights from the itinerary before booking.

---

## README alignment

This request matches the **multi-leg / itinerary** direction called out in the consolidated roadmap:

- **[README §5 — Booking Wizard and Digital Boarding Pass](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#5-booking-wizard-and-digital-boarding-pass)** — multi-step journey, review, and confirmation fit a trip-builder flow.
- **[README §13 — Travel Agency Mode](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#13-travel-agency-mode)** — explicitly mentions a path toward **multi-segment trips** alongside multi-seat booking.

Keep issue titles and acceptance criteria here as the working spec; treat the README sections above as the high-level product framing so planning stays consistent.

---

- #6 — [Feature: Travel agency mode and multi-seat booking](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/issues/6) (multi-segment direction)

title: Feature: Traveler Profile and Preferences
author: Max-Jesch
body:
# Feature: Traveler Profile and Preferences

**Problem:**
The booking process is repetitive and impersonal. Users must re-enter common information like their home planet, seat preferences, and other personal details for every new booking. This makes the process slower and less user-friendly than it could be.

**Proposed Solution:**
Introduce a "Traveler Profile" page where users can save their personal information and travel preferences. This would create a centralized location for managing details that do not change often, making future bookings faster and more personalized.

The profile should store:

- Home Planet (for pre-filling departure/arrival searches)
- Default Seat Class (e.g., Economy, Business, Galaxium Class)
- Dietary and accessibility notes (to be included with bookings)
- Emergency contact information

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Users can navigate to a dedicated "Profile" page.
- Users can input, save, and update their home planet, default seat class, dietary/accessibility notes, and an emergency contact.
- When a user makes a new booking, saved preferences (like seat class) are automatically applied as defaults.
- All personal information is stored securely.
- The booking confirmation includes any relevant dietary or accessibility notes.

---

## README alignment

This is not a standalone numbered item in **[Consolidated Implementation Ideas](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#consolidated-implementation-ideas)**, but it fits naturally next to:

- **[README §5 — Booking Wizard and Digital Boarding Pass](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#5-booking-wizard-and-digital-boarding-pass)** — saved profile data can pre-fill wizard steps.
- **[README §7 — Enterprise Authentication, Roles, and Support Workspace](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#7-enterprise-authentication-roles-and-support-workspace)** — richer identity and traveler records align with enterprise auth and support tooling later.

Use this issue for traveler-centric persistence; use §7 issues for org-wide identity and roles.

title: Feature: Travel agency mode and multi-seat booking
author: Max-Jesch
body:
# Feature: Travel agency mode and multi-seat booking

**Canonical framing:** [README.md — §13. Travel Agency Mode](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#13-travel-agency-mode)

Extend the booking experience beyond individual travelers so registered agencies can act on behalf of clients: maintain a client list, book under the correct passenger names, and reserve **multiple seats in one go** (same flight and class, with a path toward groups and multi-segment trips).

- **Why it matters:** Today the product assumes you are booking for yourself; agencies need delegation, batch seat purchases, and clear separation between the **billing agency** and each **traveling passenger**.
- **What it demonstrates:** Distinct actor types (traveler vs agency), passenger manifests, multi-seat and bulk booking APIs, inventory checks across quantity, optional agency–client approvals, and reporting sliced by agency and by client.
- **Possible UX:** Agency profile and dashboard, “Book for a client” flow with passenger details and seat count, cart-style review before confirm, per-client booking history, and confirmations that list every passenger on the reservation.

**Demo-first priority:** Listed as **#6** in [Suggested Demo-First Priority](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#suggested-demo-first-priority).

---

## Consumer scenario: family and group travel

The following remains a concrete, consumer-facing slice of the same **multi-seat manifest** problem (one primary booker, many passengers on one flight).

**Problem:** Users can only book individual seats one at a time. Families and groups need a streamlined way to book multiple seats on the same flight in a single transaction.

**Proposed solution (summary):**

1. Select a flight and specify the number of passengers (e.g. 2–10 travelers).
2. Enter passenger details for each traveler in the group.
3. Book all seats together in a single transaction.
4. Ensure seat availability for the entire group before confirming.
5. One primary booker manages the group reservation.

### Technical approach (historical notes)

**Backend (conceptual):**

- Extend booking model to support group bookings with a `group_id` field.
- Add `group_size` (or derive from manifest rows).
- Adjust booking service to handle multiple passengers atomically.
- Validate sufficient seats for the whole group.

**Frontend (conceptual):**

- Passenger count selector on the booking flow.
- Multi-step form for each passenger.
- Group summary before confirmation.
- “My Bookings” shows grouped members.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can select multiple passengers when booking a flight (within agreed limits).
- [ ] System validates that sufficient seats are available for the entire group.
- [ ] All passenger details can be entered in a single flow.
- [ ] Group bookings are created atomically (all succeed or all fail).
- [ ] Group bookings are visually grouped on the "My Bookings" page.
- [ ] Canceling a group booking cancels all associated bookings (or defines clear partial rules).
- [ ] Backend API supports multi-passenger / group creation.
- [ ] Frontend surfaces clear errors when group booking fails.
- [ ] Tests cover success, partial availability, and validation paths.

### Later / out of scope for an initial slice

- Payment splitting among group members.
- Add/remove passengers after booking.
- Seat map selection so groups sit together (see README §4 — seat selection and holds).
- Per-passenger notification flows.

### Related README sections

- **[README §4 — Seat Selection, Holds, and Concurrency Safety](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#4-seat-selection-holds-and-concurrency-safety)** — seat map and holds interact with multi-seat checkout.

---

- #4 — [Trip Builder for Multi-Leg Itineraries](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/issues/4)

title: Flight detail page (/flights/:id)
author: Max-Jesch
body:
> Tier 1, item 1 of the [Product Backlog](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#-product-backlog).

Make flight cards clickable. The detail page has a route header, ship info, per-class amenities grid, baggage and cancellation policies, and a mission timeline (launch → transfer burn → orbital insertion → landing) with a prominent "Book this flight" CTA.

### Gap
Cards aren't clickable today. There is nowhere for amenities, policies, or any richer flight context to live.

### Scope
- New route + page.
- Amenities and policies live as static config keyed by class.
- Mission-timeline milestones computed from `departure_time` and `arrival_time`.
- **Out of scope:** editable content, per-flight amenity overrides.

### Touches
- New `booking_system_frontend/src/pages/FlightDetail.tsx`
- Router in `booking_system_frontend/src/App.tsx`
- Link from `booking_system_frontend/src/components/flights/FlightCard.tsx`
- Optional ship/aircraft fields in `booking_system_backend/models.py`

### Size
~2–3 hours

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Flight cards on `/flights` are clickable and navigate to `/flights/:id`
- [ ] Detail page shows full route header (origin → destination, dates, duration)
- [ ] Per-class amenities grid renders for Economy, Business, and Galaxium
- [ ] Baggage and cancellation policy sections visible
- [ ] Mission timeline shows at least 4 milestones with relative times
- [ ] "Book this flight" CTA opens the existing booking modal
- [ ] Direct navigation to `/flights/:id` for a non-existent ID shows a friendly not-found state

title: Real passenger details in booking flow
author: Max-Jesch
body:
> Tier 1, item 3 of the [Product Backlog](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#-product-backlog).

Add a "Passenger details" step to the booking modal: full legal name, DOB, passport/ID number, contact phone, emergency contact, dietary preference.

### Gap
Every booking today carries only `user.name` and `user.email`. A multi-million-credit interplanetary flight with no ID collection feels wrong the moment anyone looks at the flow.

### Scope
- New step between "select class" and "quote" in `BookingModal.tsx`.
- Stored on the booking as a `passenger_details` JSON column *or* in a new `Passenger` table — the latter is preferred because it sets up #28.
- Required fields validated client-side (name, DOB, passport, phone).
- **Out of scope:** verification against a real ID provider.

### Touches
- `booking_system_frontend/src/components/bookings/BookingModal.tsx` (new step)
- `booking_system_backend/models.py` (`Passenger` table or column)
- `booking_system_backend/services/booking.py`
- Schema seeding

### Size
~2 hours

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New "Passenger details" step appears before the quote step
- [ ] Fields: full legal name, DOB, passport/ID number, contact phone, emergency contact (name + phone), dietary preference
- [ ] Client-side validation blocks Continue until required fields are valid
- [ ] Passenger details persist to DB and round-trip to My Trip (#26)
- [ ] Existing bookings without passenger details still render without error
- [ ] Unit tests cover the new service-layer paths

title: Multi-passenger booking (up to 6 per reservation)
author: Max-Jesch
body:

Expose the hold service's existing `quantity` field. "Add passenger" in the modal adds another passenger-details form; the price total updates live; one booking covers up to 6 passengers.

Users can only book one seat at a time. No family trips, no group travel. The backend hold service already accepts a quantity — the frontend just doesn't use it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Remove passenger" available per row (min 1)

title: Mock payment step at end of booking flow
author: Max-Jesch
body:
> Tier 1, item 5 of the [Product Backlog](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#-product-backlog).

A credit-card form at the end of the booking flow with Luhn check, expiry and CVV validation, and a billing ZIP. Fake "Processing…" spinner, fake authorization code, store last-4 and card brand on the booking.

### Gap
Users currently click "Confirm Booking" and own a reservation. There is no payment step at all — the single most jarring omission for a new user.

### Scope
- Client-side validation (Luhn, expiry in future, CVV format by brand).
- Backend `POST /payments/authorize` stub that always succeeds after a 1–2s delay.
- Store `payment_last4`, `payment_brand`, `payment_auth_code`, `paid_at` on booking.
- **Out of scope:** real PSP integration, 3DS, saved cards, refund-side flows.

### Touches
- New `booking_system_frontend/src/components/bookings/PaymentStep.tsx`
- New `booking_system_backend/services/payment.py` (stub)
- `booking_system_backend/models.py` (payment columns on Booking)

### Size
~2–3 hours

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Payment step appears after hold confirm, before final booking confirmation
- [ ] Form fields: card number, cardholder name, expiry (MM/YY), CVV, billing ZIP
- [ ] Luhn check blocks invalid card numbers

title: Refund preview on cancel
author: Max-Jesch
body:
> Tier 3, item 19 of the [Product Backlog](https://github.com/IBM/galaxium-travels/blob/main/README.md#-product-backlog).

The cancel modal shows "$X refund, $Y fee, $Z kept as travel credit" before confirming, with real cancellation-policy wording.

Standard travel-site tiers:
- 7+ days out → full refund
- 3–6 days → 75% refund + 10% fee + 15% travel credit
- 1–2 days → no refund + 25% fee + 25% travel credit
- same-day → no refund, no fee, no credit (total forfeit)

### Gap
Today's cancel modal just says "are you sure?" Real travel sites always show you what you'll get back before you confirm.

### Scope
- Backend-owned policy logic via a new \`GET /bookings/{id}/cancellation-preview\` endpoint; frontend fetches and displays the breakdown.
- **Out of scope:** actual refund processing (payment system is a stub).

### Touches
- \`MyBookings.tsx\` cancel modal
- New backend service function + \`GET /bookings/{id}/cancellation-preview\` endpoint + MCP tool
- \`booking_system_frontend/src/services/api.ts\` (new \`getCancellationPreview\` call)

### Size
~1 hour

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cancel modal shows refund / fee / credit breakdown before confirm
- [ ] Breakdown varies by days-to-departure per documented policy
- [ ] Wording is clear and product-appropriate
- [ ] Policy helper is unit-tested in the backend

### Design notes
The breakdown block should feel like a real travel site, not a debug dump. A few things that help:
- A **policy tier badge** (e.g. "Full Refund ✓" or "Non-refundable") at the top of the block so the user knows their situation at a glance before reading the numbers
- A **segmented proportion bar** showing refund / fee / credit as colour-coded bands across the full price — makes the split visually immediate without arithmetic
- A **"You'll receive back" summary row** at the bottom, separated by a divider, showing the net cash refund so the user doesn't have to add it up themselves
- **Per-row icons** (e.g. arrow-return for refund, x-circle for fee, ticket for credit) to make each line scannable

### Implementation notes
- Departure time format varies by data source — test fixtures use \`"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"\` but the live DB stores ISO 8601 with a UTC suffix (\`"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"\`). The preview service must handle both; a single \`strptime\` pattern will silently break on real data. At minimum handle: \`%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\`, \`%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S\`, \`%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\`. Write at least one test using the exact format from \`seed.py\`.
- \`GET /bookings/{id}/cancellation-preview\` must be registered in \`server.py\` **before** the existing \`GET /bookings/{user_id}\` route — FastAPI matches in registration order and the wildcard will shadow the two-segment path otherwise.

If the preview fails to load, the modal shows an inline error and still lets the user cancel. `cancel_booking` is unchanged and no money moves, so refund processing is a follow-up issue. All seed flights are in 2099, so unit tests inject "now" and the demo seed gains one or two near-term flights to show the other tiers.

## Key Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Preview fetch failure in the modal | Show an inline error and still allow cancelling | A preview bug (network, unparseable `departure_time`) must never trap a user in a booking |
| Preview vs. actual cancel | Label the breakdown "Estimated". Leave `cancel_booking` unchanged. Log refund processing as a follow-up issue | Payment is a stub, so the UI must not imply money moves. This also keeps the change minimal |
| Demonstrating and testing non-"Full refund" tiers | Unit tests inject `now`. Seed one or two near-term flights (e.g. +2 and +5 days) for the demo | Seed flights are all in 2099, so the live UI would only ever show "Full refund" |
| 1–2 day tier percentages | 0% refund / 50% fee / 50% credit | The issue's 25%/25% adds up to only 50%, so it is treated as a typo and every tier sums to 100% |
| Policy location | Backend helper plus service function; frontend only renders | One tested source of truth, and the MCP tool gets the same logic |
| Departure-time parsing | Accept `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M`, `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S` and `...Z`. Treat naive values as UTC | The seed uses `Z` ISO strings, tests use space-separated strings, and the only existing parser would fail on seed data |

## Open Items

- Seeding near-term flights changes demo data. Check that `seed.py` and any tests or e2e flows that count flights or assume 2099 dates still pass.
- Seeded near-term flights will age: "+2 days" is relative to seed time, and `SEED_DEMO_DATA=true` re-seeds on every start. Confirm the seed computes dates relative to now rather than hardcoding them.
- Wording for the tier badge labels and policy text is a draft and needs a review in the UI.
- Whether the modal needs to grow from `sm` to fit the breakdown block.
- Refund and credit processing (real payment, recording amounts on the booking) is out of scope. File a follow-up issue.
- The frontend has no unit-test runner, so the UI is verified by typecheck, lint, build and a manual browser check.

## Next Steps

1. Backend: add the `CancellationPreview` schema, the departure-time parser, the policy helper and `get_cancellation_preview(db, booking_id, now=None)` in `services/booking.py`. Return `ErrorResponse` for `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_CANCELLED` and an invalid date.
2. Backend tests: tier boundaries (7, 6, 3, 2, 1 days, same day and already departed), parts summing to `price_paid`, all three date formats, service error cases, and REST 200/404/409 tests.
3. Backend endpoint: add `GET /bookings/{booking_id}/cancellation-preview` in `server.py` above `get_user_bookings` and above `FastApiMCP(app)`. Set the response model and a docstring that states the policy tiers.
4. Seed: add one or two near-term flights (about +2 and +5 days) to `seed.py` so the partial and non-refundable tiers show up in the demo.
5. Frontend types and API: add the `CancellationPreview` type and `getCancellationPreview` in `api.ts`.
6. Frontend UI: add a `CancellationBreakdown` component with a tier badge, a segmented bar, per-row icons, a "You'll receive back" row and an "Estimated" label. Handle loading and error states, still allow cancelling on error, and reset state on close.
7. Verify with the `verify` skill (ruff, mypy, pytest, `tsc -b`, eslint, build), then check the modal manually against `./start.sh`.
8. Open a follow-up issue for actual refund processing.

title: Unified Pricing & Quote-Booking Consistency
author: Max-Jesch
body:
## Problem
Flight prices are currently inconsistent across the customer booking journey:
- **Explore page:** Calculates seat class prices via Python `_flight_to_out()` (`base_price \times [1.0, 2.5, 5.0]`).
- **Quote modal:** Calculates prices via Java `PricingService.calculatePrice()` using hardcoded flat base tables (`{economy: 500k, business: 2.5M, first: 5M}`) and an arbitrary `flightId % 3` multiplier.
- **Seat Class naming:** Java uses legacy `"first"` instead of `"galaxium"`, causing Galaxium quotes to default to economy base pricing.
- **Booking price discrepancy:** `HoldService.confirmHold()` omits the quoted price when calling Python's `/internal/bookings/from-hold`. Python recalculates the price from scratch, writing a different value to the DB than what was quoted.

## Specification & PRD
See full PRD in [`docs/requirements/price-quote-consistency.md`](docs/requirements/price-quote-consistency.md).

## Core Requirements
1. **Single Source of Truth:** Python backend serves as the authoritative pricing source. Java `PricingService` queries or synchronizes with Python rather than using disconnected hardcoded tables.
2. **Domain Alignment:** Standardize seat classes across all services on `economy`, `business`, and `galaxium`.
3. **Lock Quoted Price on Hold:** Java forwards `pricePaid` and `quoteId` when confirming a hold to `/internal/bookings/from-hold`.
4. **Honor Quoted Price at Booking:** Python persists the locked quoted price in `Booking.price_paid`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Catalog price on Explore page matches the quote modal price breakdown for all flights and seat classes.
- [ ] Creating a quote for `"galaxium"` class applies the 5.0x multiplier and succeeds.
- [ ] Confirmed booking `price_paid` strictly matches the quote's `total_price`.
- [ ] Removed arbitrary `flightId % 3` modulo jitter from quote pricing.
- [ ] E2E test suite passes.
